A driver touched a memory address it was: A driver touched a memory address it was not allowed to at that moment. Almost always a third-party driver (network, audio, RGB, antivirus); less often unstable RAM.
A kernel memory block was corrupted. Typ: A kernel memory block was corrupted. Typical causes: a faulty third-party driver (antivirus, VPN, RGB) or unstable RAM (XMP/EXPO profile).
Windows' memory manager found a serious: Windows' memory manager found a serious inconsistency. Very often RAM (aggressive XMP/EXPO profile, failing stick), sometimes a driver.
A kernel component (driver) raised an er: A kernel component (driver) raised an error it did not handle. Parameter 2 points straight into the faulting driver.
The NTFS file system hit an error: faili: The NTFS file system hit an error: failing disk, faulty SATA cable or volume corruption. Run chkdsk and check SMART.
An error occurred during a system call. Parameter 2 is the faulting instruction, often in a graphics driver, anti-cheat or antivirus.
The page frame database is corrupted. Mo: The page frame database is corrupted. Most often unstable or failing RAM; more rarely a driver freeing the same memory twice.
The kernel accessed memory that does not: The kernel accessed memory that does not exist. Parameter 3 points to the faulting instruction. Causes: buggy driver, antivirus, or unstable RAM.
Windows could not read back a kernel mem: Windows could not read back a kernel memory page from disk. Sign of a failing SSD/disk, cable or unstable controller.
Windows cannot reach its boot disk: SATA: Windows cannot reach its boot disk: SATA/RAID mode changed in BIOS, failed storage driver update or failing disk.
A system thread crashed and was not caug: A system thread crashed and was not caught. Parameter 2 points into the responsible driver (often graphics, Wi-Fi or a recently installed driver).
The CPU raised a trap the kernel could n: The CPU raised a trap the kernel could not handle (often a stack overflow). Leads: CPU overclock/undervolt, RAM, very low-level driver.
An unhandled exception in kernel mode. P: An unhandled exception in kernel mode. Parameter 2 is the faulting address. Third-party driver or unstable RAM.
The CPU detected a fatal hardware error: The CPU detected a fatal hardware error (older equivalent of WHEA). Overclock, voltage, temperature or motherboard.
A driver did not respond during sleep or: A driver did not respond during sleep or wake. Very common with Wi-Fi, USB and graphics drivers; Fast Startup often makes it worse.
Internal power-management error, often t: Internal power-management error, often tied to hibernation or Fast Startup.
A driver tried to write to read-only mem: A driver tried to write to read-only memory: buggy or malicious driver.
A driver misused kernel memory (double f: A driver misused kernel memory (double free, bad size). Almost always software.
Windows Driver Verifier caught a driver: Windows Driver Verifier caught a driver misbehaving. If you enabled it, turn it off (verifier /reset) after noting the culprit.
A driver corrupted kernel memory. Parame: A driver corrupted kernel memory. Parameter 4 points into the driver that touched it.
A driver accessed invalid memory at a cr: A driver accessed invalid memory at a critical moment. Parameter 4 points into that driver: network (Realtek, Killer, Intel), audio or USB most often.
The graphics driver got stuck waiting fo: The graphics driver got stuck waiting for the card. Predecessor of TDR: GPU driver, power or overheating.
A process Windows cannot live without st: A process Windows cannot live without stopped. Corrupted system files, SSD dropping out (NVMe) or overzealous antivirus.
A critical process was terminated, often: A critical process was terminated, often because the system disk stopped responding (SSD, cable, controller).
A driver tried to execute code from non-: A driver tried to execute code from non-executable memory: buggy driver or memory corruption.
Fatal error in the USB stack: faulty USB: Fatal error in the USB stack: faulty USB device, hub or USB controller driver.
A CPU core stopped responding. Almost al: A CPU core stopped responding. Almost always hardware: CPU overclock/undervolt, voltage, old BIOS, failing CPU.
The kernel detected forbidden changes to: The kernel detected forbidden changes to its structures (PatchGuard): cheat or low-level monitoring driver, or failing RAM.
Internal video memory management error:: Internal video memory management error: graphics driver, unstable VRAM (GPU memory overclock) or HAGS.
Windows' graphics kernel (DirectX) hit a: Windows' graphics kernel (DirectX) hit a fatal error, often after a botched GPU driver update.
The graphics card stopped responding and: The graphics card stopped responding and Windows could not restart its driver. GPU driver, MPO, aggressive undervolt/overclock, power supply or PCIe cable. Parameter 2 points into the graphics driver.
The graphics card did not respond in tim: The graphics card did not respond in time; Windows restarted the driver successfully this time. Same causes as 0x116, less severe.
The graphics scheduler detected an incon: The graphics scheduler detected an inconsistency: GPU driver, HAGS or card overclock.
The hardware reported an uncorrectable e: The hardware reported an uncorrectable error: CPU (overclock, undervolt, Curve Optimizer), RAM, PCIe link or power supply. Not a driver problem.
A memory page was corrupted by hardware:: A memory page was corrupted by hardware: failing or unstable RAM.
A driver hogged the CPU for too long. Cl: A driver hogged the CPU for too long. Classics: old NVMe SSD firmware, storage/SATA driver, audio or network driver.
The kernel detected corruption of its da: The kernel detected corruption of its data structures (buffer overrun). Third-party driver, anti-cheat or unstable RAM.
The kernel heap was corrupted by a drive: The kernel heap was corrupted by a driver. Often a graphics, audio or RGB device driver.
Fatal USB 3 driver error: device, hub, c: Fatal USB 3 driver error: device, hub, cable or USB power saving.
The compressed memory store hit an error: The compressed memory store hit an error, often because of the disk (SSD dropping out, bad sectors) or an antivirus.
The power button was held down: Windows: The power button was held down: Windows wrote this dump to diagnose a frozen PC.
Intentionally triggered crash (keyboard: Intentionally triggered crash (keyboard shortcut or diagnostic tool).
The GPU stopped responding and Windows f:
The GPU stopped responding and Windows failed to reset the graphics driver. Video signal cuts immediately (black screen) and GPU fans spin to 100%.
Solutions: Disable MPO, disable Skia Graphite (Chrome/Edge), disable ULPS on AMD, raise TdrDelay to 10s, and check 750-850 mV points if GPU undervolted.
The secure kernel (virtualization-based: The secure kernel (virtualization-based security, Memory Integrity) detected an error. Already caused by a Windows update (April 2025) and by drivers incompatible with Memory Integrity: install the latest updates and update the drivers flagged in Windows Security.
